nodes.label: Measured Country Distribution (US/India/France)
nodes.rationale: Train is US/India only (~60/40); test shifts to ~38% US, ~47% India, ~15% France — a distribution shift as well as a zero-shot country.

nodes.label: Dataset Description (Measured Stats)
nodes.rationale: All statistics were measured directly from the files rather than copied from the problem statement; companion to README.md and PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md.

nodes.label: France as Zero-Shot Country
nodes.rationale: No training labels exist for France, so any country-conditioned model or threshold must degrade gracefully to a country-agnostic fallback; hold out one train country to approximate unseen-country generalisation.

nodes.label: Template §3: Candidate Generation (Blocking)
nodes.rationale: Requires documenting blocking keys (e.g. PIN code, phonetic encoding, TF-IDF), candidate pair totals, and how true matches were preserved.

nodes.label: Template §4: Matching Model
nodes.rationale: Requires documenting name features, address features, model type (e.g. XGBoost, Siamese Network, Transformer) and threshold selection method such as F_0.5 optimization on validation.

nodes.label: Solution Documentation Template
nodes.rationale: Mandatory methodology write-up template (executive summary, methodology, blocking, matching model, results/error analysis, conclusion, appendices) shipped in the submission zip; teams may modify sections while keeping clarity and technical depth.

nodes.label: Blocking / Candidate Generation
nodes.rationale: A strong blocking strategy determines the upper bound of recall; it is the stage that reduces the comparison space before the matching model scores candidate pairs.

nodes.label: External Data Lookup Prohibition
nodes.rationale: Strictly prohibited: commercial ER APIs, government registries, geocoding APIs or any internet data augmentation; violation means immediate disqualification, because the challenge must test ML skills using only the provided training data.

nodes.label: Open-Set Country Rule
nodes.rationale: Country must be treated as an open set of string labels: do not hard-code, filter, or one-hot to {US, India}, because the test set adds France and every test entity must appear in the submission.

nodes.label: ML Challenge 2026 Problem Statement (README)
nodes.rationale: Condensed version of the official problem statement covering data format, output format, constraints, evaluation and fair play.

nodes.label: Injective Ground-Truth Mapping
nodes.rationale: No S2/S3 ID is claimed by two S1 entities (0 of 7,638,365 matched IDs shared), making the mapping injective on the S2/S3 side; all referenced IDs exist in their source files.

nodes.label: One-to-One Assignment Prior
nodes.rationale: Because no S2/S3 record is shared between S1 entities, a stable-matching or greedy assignment filter (each S2/S3 assigned to its highest-scoring S1) can be applied after thresholding without external data — but only if it does not lower validation macro F_0.5.

nodes.label: Business Entity Resolution Challenge
nodes.rationale: Business identity data arrives from multiple independent sources as partial, noisy fragments with no common identifiers; the ML task is to determine which records across 3 sources refer to the same real-world business.

nodes.label: train_ground_truth.tsv
nodes.rationale: Two columns (source1_entity_id, matched_entity_ids); labels exist only for training, so self-evaluation requires holding out a validation split scored with the F_0.5 formula.

nodes.label: Source 1 (Deduplicated Reference Source)
nodes.rationale: Source 1 is the deduplicated reference source; every S1 entity must be output once, and it may match zero, one, or many S2/S3 records.

nodes.label: TSV / Comma / Encoding Reading Gotchas
nodes.rationale: Commas appear inside business_address and matched_entity_ids, so always use sep="\t"; use keep_default_na=False or dtype=str so empty addresses stay "" instead of NaN; normalize country with strip().lower() but never filter on it.

nodes.label: Template Appendix A: Code Artefacts
nodes.rationale: Code ships in code/business_entity_resolution/ with all source in src/, README.md and requirements.txt; the appendix summarises structure and entry points that reproduce output/matching_results.tsv and output/candidate_pairs.tsv.

nodes.label: candidate_pairs.tsv
nodes.rationale: The last blocking/filtering stage output — the exact candidate set fed to the matching model. Not scored on the leaderboard; used to analyse blocking quality (recall ceiling, reduction ratio) and verify the pipeline. Final matches must be a subset of candidates.

nodes.label: matching_results.tsv
nodes.rationale: The only file scored on the leaderboard; one row per S1 entity, matched_entity_ids is a comma-separated S2/S3 ID list (empty for singletons) with no duplicates.

nodes.label: Final Submission Package (zip)
nodes.rationale: Single zip containing output/ (matching_results.tsv, candidate_pairs.tsv), code/business_entity_resolution/ (src, README, requirements.txt) and the filled Documentation_template.md; used to reproduce results, audit blocking, and check fair-play/licence rules.

nodes.label: utils/validate_submission.py
nodes.rationale: Stdlib-only helper that checks both output files against all submission rules, printing PASS (exit 0) or a numbered list of issues (exit 1); it does not compute the score.

nodes.label: Singletons: 5.585% of Train S1 Entities
nodes.rationale: 123,247 of 2,206,821 train S1 entities have empty match lists; under macro F_0.5 each correctly-empty prediction scores 1.0 and each false merge 0.0, so they carry about 5.6% of the score on their own.

nodes.label: F_0.5 Score (β = 0.5)
nodes.rationale: Precision-heavy metric chosen because merging two distinct businesses (false positive) is more damaging than missing a link (false negative); F_0.5 weights precision 2x over recall and is macro-averaged per S1 entity with singletons included.

nodes.label: Singleton Scoring (no true matches)
nodes.rationale: A Source 1 entity with no true matches scores 1.0 for a correctly predicted empty list and 0.0 for any predicted match, so singletons must not be neglected in threshold tuning.

nodes.label: Missing business_address (~3.3% of S2/S3)
nodes.rationale: 168,967 train S2 (3.36%) and 175,916 train S3 (3.33%) addresses are empty; such candidates have only a name signal, so features need address_missing flags and must avoid division by zero.

nodes.label: Non-Latin Script Names (~15% of Train S2)
nodes.norm_label: non-latin script names (~15% of train s2)
nodes.rationale: Source 1 train names are 100% ASCII while 15.19% of train S2 names (Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Malayalam) are non-Latin, so cross-script matching is required; pure edit distance is weak and phonetic/transliteration-insensitive features matter.

nodes.label: UTF-8 Files / cp1252 Console Artifact
nodes.rationale: All files are valid UTF-8 with no literal ??? placeholders; the ??????-looking names seen in a Windows console are real non-Latin script misrendered through cp1252, and L�arning is correctly encoded Léarning.

nodes.label: Noise Patterns (Name & Address Variations)
nodes.rationale: Expected noise: abbreviations (Corp/Corporation, Pvt/Private, Ltd/Limited, Rd/Road, St/Street), legal-suffix inconsistency, DBA/trade names, punctuation (& vs and), word-order transpositions, typos, transliterations, missing address components, landmark-based references, municipal numbering formats.
